verifications.claim: The Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA) of 1978 is a U.S. federal law.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: FISA was initially enacted in 1978 (R1); The Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court was established by Congress in 1978 (R2); Congress enacted FISA in 1978 (R3); established under the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978 (FISA) (R4); Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978 (R11)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state FISA was enacted in 1978 as U.S. federal law.

verifications.claim: FISA establishes procedures for physical and electronic surveillance of foreign intelligence on domestic soil.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: sets out procedures for physical and electronic surveillance and collection of foreign intelligence information (R1); FISA provides a statutory framework under which the federal government can seek and receive court authorization to conduct electronic surveillance to collect foreign intelligence information in the United States (R3); regulates a number of the most sensitive types of intelligence collection activities that occur within the United States (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly describe FISA procedures for physical and electronic surveillance for foreign intelligence domestically.

verifications.claim: FISA established the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court (FISC).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: FISA also established the United States Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court (FISC) (R1); The Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court was established by Congress in 1978 (R2); FISA created the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court (FISC) (R3); established under the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978 (FISA) (R4); Congress created in 1978 when it enacted the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA) (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Direct statements confirm FISA established FISC.

verifications.claim: FISC oversees warrant requests primarily targeting foreign powers and agents.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: consider issuing search warrants under FISA... probable cause to believe that the "target of the surveillance is a foreign power or agent of a foreign power" (R1); oversee requests for surveillance warrants against foreign spies inside the United States (R4); probable cause to believe that the target is a foreign power... or an agent of a foreign power (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm FISC reviews warrants targeting foreign powers/agents.

verifications.claim: Section 702 allows warrantless targeting of non-U.S. persons outside the U.S.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: authorizes U.S. government surveillance of non-U.S. persons abroad... does not have to seek court authorization for every individual it targets (R3); authorized to target non-U.S. persons who are reasonably believed to be located outside the United States (R5); authorizes the government to surveil foreigners located outside the United States (R6); no individual FISC order is required for each target (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation of warrantless targeting of non-U.S. persons abroad.

verifications.claim: Section 702 often captures Americans' data.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: incidental collection entails U.S.-person communications that are collected in the course of targeting non-U.S. persons... in large volumes (R3, R6); communications of U.S. persons are sometimes incidentally acquired (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe incidental collection of U.S. persons' data as common/large volume, supporting 'often'.

verifications.claim: FISA was enacted to prevent illegal warrantless surveillance of Americans.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: congressional investigations into Federal surveillance activities conducted in the name of national security... to provide judicial and congressional oversight (R1); response to concerns regarding warrantless surveillance of individuals in the United States by the executive branch (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly links enactment to addressing warrantless surveillance abuses.

verifications.claim: FISA authorizes, limits, and regulates surveillance for foreign intelligence gathering.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: establish procedures for the authorization of electronic surveillance... physical searches... for the purpose of gathering foreign intelligence (R1); statutory framework... to conduct electronic surveillance to collect foreign intelligence information (R3); legal tools... to collect foreign intelligence information while protecting privacy (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe FISA as authorizing/regulating with oversight/limits.

verifications.claim: FISC is a specialized court.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: The Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court (R2); a U.S. federal court established... to oversee requests for surveillance warrants (R4); The U.S. Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court (FISC) is a specialized federal court (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Directly called 'specialized' or described as such for FISA purposes.

verifications.claim: FISC reviews and approves applications for surveillance warrants and physical searches.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: consider issuing search warrants under FISA (R1); reviews requests to conduct physical and electronic surveillance (R4); review... applications for authorization to employ various means... electronic surveillance (Title I of FISA) and physical search (Title III) (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Explicit review/approval role for warrants and searches.

verifications.claim: Under Section 702, FISC reviews targeting procedures.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: FISC must review the aforementioned submission [certification specifying the surveillance procedures]... targeting procedures (R3); FISA Court approving... targeting and minimization procedures (R5); FISC must approve special procedures... targeted at non-U.S. persons (R7); reviews Section 702 applications... targeting, minimization, and querying procedures (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm FISC reviews targeting procedures for 702.

verifications.claim: Section 702 allows targeting of non-U.S. persons located outside the U.S. to gather foreign intelligence.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: target non-U.S. persons abroad... to acquire foreign intelligence information (R3); target non-U.S. persons... located outside the United States to acquire foreign intelligence information (R5); surveil foreigners located outside the United States (R6); targeting of non-U.S. persons located outside the United States to collect foreign intelligence information (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Precise match across sources.

verifications.claim: Section 702 often involves US electronic communication service providers.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: collecting foreign intelligence information from domestic electronic communications systems... direct electronic communication service providers (ECSPs) (R3); collection of communications by foreign persons that utilize U.S. communications service providers (R5); compel U.S. companies to assist in the targeting (R7)
verifications.reasoning: 'Often' supported by description as principal method.

verifications.claim: Section 702 does not require an individual warrant for each target.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: does not have to seek court authorization for every individual it targets... authorized programmatically rather than individually (R3); no individual FISC order is required for each target (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Direct statement on no individual warrants.

verifications.claim: Section 702 relies on court-approved targeting and minimization procedures, as detailed on Intelligence.gov.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: certification specifying the surveillance procedures... targeting individuals for surveillance, minimizing... FISC must review (R3); approving such a certification and the use of targeting and minimization procedures (R5); FISC must approve special procedures that ensure... targeted... “minimized” (R7 from Intelligence.gov)
verifications.reasoning: R7 is Intelligence.gov; directly details court-approved procedures.

verifications.claim: FISA has been amended in 2008.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: FISA (Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act) Amendments Act of 2008 (R1); added Section 702 to FISA in 2008 as part of the FISA Amendments Act of 2008 (R3); amended in 2008 by the FISA Amendments Act (R11)
verifications.reasoning: Explicit 2008 amendments confirmed.

verifications.claim: As of April 2026, Congress is debating the reauthorization of Section 702.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Section 702 will sunset on April 20, 2026... Congress's deliberation on whether to reauthorize (R3); Congress will soon vote on the reauthorization... set to expire on April 20 (R6); key tool... will expire this month [April 2026 context] (R9); FISA dies unless SAVE America is attached [April 2026 context] (R10)
verifications.reasoning: Sources from April 2026 discuss ongoing reauthorization debate before April 20 sunset.

verifications.claim: Section 702 is set to expire on April 20.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Section 702 will sunset on April 20, 2026 (R3); set to expire on April 20 (R6); set to expire on April 20 (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources specify April 20 expiration (contextually 2026).

verifications.claim: Some lawmakers are proposing attaching the Save America Act.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Rep. Anna Paulina Luna (R-Fla.) said... FISA dies unless SAVE America is attached... looking to leverage the renewal of Section 702... to advance the SAVE America Act
verifications.reasoning: Direct quote from lawmaker proposing attachment.

verifications.claim: The Save America Act would add a requirement of proof of citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: The SAVE America Act... would require proof of citizenship to register to vote in federal elections
verifications.reasoning: Exact match to claim.

verifications.claim: The Save America Act would add a requirement of the presentation of an ID to cast a ballot
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: and the presentation of an ID to cast a ballot
verifications.reasoning: Direct statement in source.
